sources.title: NGSS 4-ESS2-1: Make observations and/or measurements to provide evidence of the effects of weathering or the rate of erosion by water, ice, wind, or vegetation
Physical Geology, H5P Edition (Earle and Panchuk, BCcampus), 8.1 Physical Weathering

note.text: Even hard rock has tiny cracks in it.

steps.title: Crack
steps.instruction: Draw the thin crack in the rock.

note.text: Rain and melting snow can seep into a crack.

steps.title: Water
steps.instruction: Dab the two drops of water falling into the crack.

note.text: Step 1: water trickles into the crack and fills it.
Step 2 shows the same rock on a freezing night.
When water freezes into ice, it expands: it takes up more space. The ice pushes the crack wider.

steps.title: Ice
steps.instruction: Trace the wedge of ice inside the crack.

note.text: Then the ice melts, more water seeps deeper in, and it freezes again. Each freeze and thaw pushes the crack a little wider.

steps.title: Broken rock
steps.instruction: Trace the two pieces in picture 3.

note.text: Step 3: after many freezes and thaws, the rock splits apart. Breaking rock down like this is called weathering.

steps.title: Arrows
steps.instruction: Draw the arrows from one picture to the next.

note.text: This happens slowly, over many cold nights and warm days.

steps.title: Steps
steps.instruction: Tap the steps of ice wedging in order.
steps.why: Water fills the crack, freezes and expands, widening it; after many freezes and thaws, the rock breaks.
steps.hint: What has to get into the crack first?

steps.title: Where?
steps.question: Where does ice wedging break rocks fastest?

options.text: A place that often freezes at night and thaws in the day
options.feedback: Yes. Each freeze widens the cracks a little, so many freeze-thaw swings break rock fastest.
It rarely freezes there, and there's little water to seep into cracks.

options.text: A place that's frozen all year
options.feedback: If it never thaws, the ice doesn't melt and refreeze, so cracks don't keep growing.
Ice wedging needs freezing. A warm place rarely freezes.
